formal.text: "Valor" has been canceled by The CW after completing its first and only season. The military drama, which followed an elite unit of U.S. Army helicopter pilots, starred Matt Barr, Christina Ochoa, Charlie Barnett, Corbin Reid, W. Tre Davis, Nigel Thatch, and Melissa Roxburgh. The series, produced by Bill Haber, Anna Fricke, and Kyle Jarrow, was a co-production between CBS Television Studios and Warner Bros. Television. "Valor" premiered as part of The CW's fall 2018 schedule but did not secure a second season. Its final season concluded in late January 2019, averaging 958,000 total viewers and a 0.21 rating among the 18-49 demographic. Notably, "Valor" outperformed The CW's new series "Dynasty" in the ratings.

formal.text: There is no specific diagnostic test for Bell's palsy. A healthcare provider will assess your facial muscles by observing your ability to perform various movements, such as closing your eyes, raising your brows, showing your teeth, and frowning. Other conditions, including strokes, infections, Lyme disease, and tumors, can also lead to similar symptoms. This test evaluates the electrical activity of muscles and the conduction of electrical impulses along nerves, aiding in confirming nerve damage.

formal.text: Travis Scott has filed a countersuit against Minnesota-based promoters Alex Martini, Jefferson Agar, and Patrick Johnston, who are accused of failing to arrange travel for his return to Los Angeles after a February 3, 2018, concert in Minneapolis. The promoters had previously sued Scott for canceling the event. Scott's attorney, Howard King, claims that the promoters breached their contract and owe Scott a balance of his fee.

emotional.text: Travis Scott is fighting back against what he calls 'wannabe promoters' who he believes wronged him. After being sued for canceling a February 3, 2018, concert in Minneapolis, Scott has filed a countersuit, alleging that the promoters, Alex Martini, Jefferson Agar, and Patrick Johnston, failed to set up travel arrangements for his return to Los Angeles. Scott's attorney, Howard King, refers to the promoters as 'three wannabe promoters' and accuses them of breaching their contract, leaving Scott owed a balance of his fee.
